gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'extra watts' figures are three different things: EcoFlow's 4,800 W and Jackery's 4,400 W are motor-start surge, BLUETTI's 3,900 W is a resistive-only Power Lifting mode with no surge figure on its US page, and the 3,600 W Pecron surges to only 4,500 W for 5 s, less than the 2,400 W EcoFlow.
standout_why: Compared against three pages I opened: outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000 (cited; five 2 kWh units with continuous watts only, no surge, boost, cycle life or recharge time), PopSci's Black Friday roundup (cited; continuous watts, one surge figure for the Anker S2000, and '10,000 cycles' for it with no retention percentage) and EcoFlow's Black Friday page (cited; '2400W Output | 10ms UPS' only). None separates surge from boost or puts cycle life on one yardstick. Business Insider and Popular Mechanics (both cited) refused the fetch, so I could not rule them out; that keeps this at 2, not 3.
decides: It confirms a 2 kWh pick but corrects ChatGPT's tie-break. The Elite 200 V2's real edge over the DELTA 3 Max is 200 W continuous (2,600 vs 2,400 W); its 3,900 W is for kettles and heaters and should not be set against EcoFlow's 4,800 W surge. For a fridge compressor start, the EcoFlow is the one with a published surge figure. Availability, read from the maker pages today, also cuts against the BLUETTI as the pick: Elite 200 V2 ships early January (past the four-week rule) and the Anker C2000 Gen 2 in 6-12 weeks, while the DELTA 3 Max at $879 carried no pre-order notice in the text I read, the Jackery ships by Dec 11 and the Pecron mid-December. The Pecron F3000LFP at $899 leads on Wh and continuous watts per dollar but has the thinnest start headroom (1.25x). The Elite 200 V2 honestly wins 'most continuous watts and longest stated cycle life among 2 kWh units', with its ship date in the row.

findings.label: Normalised start headroom (surge ÷ continuous, makers' figures)
findings.value: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 4,800/2,400 W = 2.0x; Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 4,400/2,200 W = 2.0x; Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 4,000/2,400 W = 1.67x; Pecron F3000LFP 4,500/3,600 W = 1.25x (5 s); BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 no surge figure on its US page (3,900 W is resistive-only Power Lifting); DJI Power 2000 no surge figure on its spec page
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Portable Power Station (2048Wh)
findings.note: My arithmetic from each maker's page; the per-product rows below carry each source. In absolute surge watts the order is EcoFlow 4,800 > Pecron 4,500 > Jackery 4,400 > Anker 4,000, so the unit with the most continuous watts does not have the most surge.

findings.value: 2,600 W continuous; Power Lifting: 'pure resistive loads of up to 3,900W'; no surge or peak figure on the page
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: The 3,900 W is 1.5x rated and applies to resistive loads only (kettles, heaters, hair dryers), so it is not comparable with a surge rating.

findings.label: Price, ship date, recharge, solar, warranty, capacity wording
findings.value: $899.00; 'expected to ship in early January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18'; 80% in 1.1 hours with TurboBoost (1,800 W AC input), 1.4 h listed for full; solar 12-60 V / 20 A, 1,000 W max; 5-year warranty; title says 2,073.6 Wh, feature list says 2,080 Wh

findings.label: Measured usable energy (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty)
findings.value: 1.91 kWh discharged, 2.44 kWh to recharge; 53.4 lb (24.2 kg); UPS 15 ms
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review
findings.note: Review dated 2025-04-25. My arithmetic: 1.91 / 2.0736 = 92% of rated capacity, matching the Popular Mechanics figure ChatGPT quoted; 1.91 / 2.44 = 78% round trip. ChatGPT's 85% assumption gives 17 h at 100 W; 1.91 kWh gives 19 h.

findings.label: A named reviewer mixes up peak and Power Lifting
findings.value: StorageReview gives '3600W peak' in its intro and says the unit 'can peak at 3,900W' in its build section
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review
findings.note: BLUETTI's own page calls 3,900 W a resistive-load mode. This shows why the footnote is needed. StorageReview also cites 'over 6,000' cycles with no retention percentage.

findings.label: Price, ship date and the surge behind 3,600 W

findings.label: AC recharge to 80%, one yardstick (makers' figures)
findings.value: Anker C2000 Gen 2 45 min; DJI Power 2000 55 min; BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 1.1 h (66 min); EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 68 min; Jackery 2000 v2 gives only 0-100% in about 1.7 h; Pecron F3000LFP gives only '2 Hours' at 1,800 W for 3,072 Wh
